title: VectorRail: collapsed panorama sidebar + temporal workspace switching prototype
creator: Amira Khan
description: Problem: Customers complain that switching contexts (workspace/project/model) is slow and noisy; cost and rollout controls are buried in separate screens and users lose routing context when switching. Goal: validate a compact, role-aware sidebar pattern (VectorRail) that preserves active route state when switching workspaces and surfaces rollouts + cost lenses in the primary nav. This ticket covers the prototype, moderated usability testing, a lightweight accessibility pass, and a handoff package for engineering. Success metrics: median workspace switch time < 1.2s (per prototype), task success >= 90% for locating rollout controls, and qualitative reduction in reported mental model friction in 5 usability sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive Figma prototype demonstrates collapsed and expanded VectorRail states with route persistence
Usability test (n=5) completed and summary uploaded with observed task times and quotes
Design spec includes ARIA patterns and motion budget guidance for engineers
Handoff bundle (Figma + token map + PRD links) posted to Confluence and referenced in GitHub ticket
Stakeholder sign-off from PM and Eng indicating rollout controls are discoverable in nav
decisions: Adopt route-preserving workspace tokens so a user moving between workspaces stays on equivalent console routes if available
Use a single, compact primary rail instead of a dual-rail approach to minimize horizontal real estate on small screens
Surface Rollouts and Cost Lenses as contextual flyouts rather than separate full-screen routes to reduce navigation hops
tradeoffs: Pros: Faster context switching, fewer full page reloads, clearer cost/rollout discoverability. Cons: More complex state management on the frontend and potential confusion for users who expect full-page settings screens.
Keeping global search in topbar preserves discoverability but reduces available vertical space in the collapsed mode.
Preferring flyouts reduces route fragmentation but may obscure history for power users who want bookmarkable URLs.
